extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance from the MPEP on what information may be required under 37 CFR 1.105 during patent examination, how and when such requirements should be made, how applicants must reply, and how examiners must handle replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: (G) Identification of pending or abandoned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of pending or abandoned applications filed by at least one of the inventors or assigned to the same assignee as the current application that disclose similar subject matter that are not otherwise identified in the current application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to require disclosure of related family or parallel filings that bear on patentability; part of enumerated examples of information that may be required under 37 CFR 1.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: (H) Reply to a matter raised in a protest (37 CFR 1.291)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to a matter raised in a protest under 37 CFR 1.291.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require applicant response to protest issues as part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: (I) Explanation of technical material in a publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of technical material in a publication, such as one of the inventor’s publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be asked to explain technical passages that are relied upon or referenced in the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: (J) Identification of changes in a reformatted continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: The identification of changes made in a reformatted continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that clarify alterations in continuation filings to ensure clear record of subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: (K) Mark-up for continuation-in-part showing added subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark-up for a continuation-in-part application showing the subject matter added where there is an intervening reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify what was added in a CIP relative to intervening art to assess written description/priority issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: (L) Comments on a new Federal Circuit decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on a new decision by the Federal Circuit that appears on point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be required to comment on new controlling case law relevant to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: (M) Publication date of an undated document
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication date of an undated document mentioned by applicant that may qualify as printed publication prior art (35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify dating to determine prior art status under 35 U.S.C. 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: (N) Comments on possible derivation (35 U.S.C. 102(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on information of record which raises a question of whether applicant derived the invention from another under 35 U.S.C. 102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where evidence suggests derivation; applicant input sought to resolve derivation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: (O) Art related to applicant’s invention/disclosure/claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Art related to applicant’s invention, applicant’s disclosure, or the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request to identify or provide art that shows context or relates to claimed subject matter to assist searching and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: (P) Other factual information pertinent to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Other factual information pertinent to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for factual matters that bear on patentability but do not fit other enumerated categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Q) Accuracy of examiner’s stated analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy of the examiner’s stated analysis of such items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may be required to point out inaccuracies in the examiner’s analysis; examiner should consider applicant’s corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: (R) Clarification/support for means/steps-plus-function claim limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification of the correlation and identification of what structure, material, or acts set forth in the specification would be capable of carrying out a function recited in a means or steps plus function claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If support for a means-plus-function limitation is not apparent and applicant cannot identify it, examiner may conclude no such support exists and make rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description) or 112 second paragraph (indefiniteness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories/Stipulations — common technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory or stipulation of the common technical features shared among all claims, or admission that certain groups of claims do not share any common technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to clarify claim relationships and commonality for examination and restriction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — support for means/steps-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112, para. 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory about the support found in the disclosure for means or steps plus function claims (35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks precise pointer to disclosure support for means-plus-function limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — written description/enablement support for claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory of precisely which portion(s) of the disclosure provide the written description and enablement support for specific claim element(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires applicant to identify exact pages/lines/figures supporting claim elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — meaning of claim limitations/terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory of the meaning of claim limitations or terms used in the claims, including what teachings in the prior art would be covered by particular limitations or dictionary definitions that would define a particular claim term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly used where terms are not used per se in the specification; clarifies claim scope for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — portions corresponding to admitted prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory of which portions of each claim correspond to any admitted prior art in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps identify what in claims is already disclosed/admitted to be prior art by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — specific utility by claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory of the specific utility provided by the claimed subject matter on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies enablement/utility issues claim-by-claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — whether dependent claim element is known in prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory as to whether a dependent claim element is known in the prior art based on the examiner having a reasonable basis for believing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks applicant admission or denial regarding prior art knowledge of dependent elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — support for added limitations in amended claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory of support for added limitations in an amended claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used after amendments to identify disclosure basis for newly added limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — facts related to public use or sale situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatory of facts related to public use or sale situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks factual detail relevant to public use/sale prior art determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When may a requirement for information be made
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is discretionary and may be made at any time once the necessity is recognized; optimum time is prior to or with a first action on the merits because examiner can best apply the response. Ordinarily, a request should not be made with or after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement should be made at earliest opportunity after necessity recognized; avoid making requests with or after final rejection; see exceptions for ongoing proceedings in issued/abandoned applications (revive, change inventorship, reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for appropriateness of making requirement prior to first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to consider for making a separate requirement prior to the first action: (A) claimed subject matter in newly established art area without well-developed prior art; (B) whether applicant submitted an IDS; (C) whether specification's background adequately describes background; (D) whether related documents by inventor/assignee not submitted are found during search; (E) whether non-patent literature is referred to but a copy not supplied; (F) whether specification’s background describes information as known/conventional but it is unfamiliar to examiner and further details are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these factors to decide narrow pre-first-action requirements (e.g., restriction requirements, expanded search domains). Emphasizes narrowly specifying requirement to avoid undue burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of making requirement with the first action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement may be combined with a first action on the merits that includes at least one rejection when the application file or lack of relevant prior art justifies asking applicant for information relevant to patentability determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not appropriate to require information based on lack of relevant prior art if first action is an allowance or Ex parte Quayle action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of making requirement after the first action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement after the first action may be appropriate when the application file justifies asking applicant for information relevant to patentability. It is rarely appropriate to require information because of lack of relevant prior art after the first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement is improper when no further examiner action would be taken; reasonable necessity implies further examiner action (generally non-final action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to requirements must be complete and timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to requirements under 37 CFR 1.105 must be complete and filed within the time period set including any extensions; failure to reply results in abandonment. Incomplete replies can be completed within original period; supplemental late replies must comply with other rules for submissions of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check replies for completeness; incomplete reply may prompt follow-up requirement when reasonable and warranted. Use form paragraph 7.95 for bona fide but non-responsive replies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to replies to 37 CFR 1.105 requirements and requires applicants to reply with information reasonably and readily available. 37 CFR 1.56's material-to-patentability threshold is higher than the reasonable necessity threshold for 1.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit information already known and reasonably available, but is not required to search for unknown information. 1.105 may require information not material to patentability but necessary to obtain complete record for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement giving either the information required or a statement that the information is unknown and/or not readily available to the party from which it was requested. Applicant must make a good faith attempt and reasonable inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No need to distinguish between 'unknown' vs 'not readily available'—either statement is acceptable after reasonable inquiry. Replies should be unambiguous; if unclear or showing misunderstanding, follow-up may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of an incomplete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply in a pending application or reexamination is handled like an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final Office action. Where reply is bona fide, form paragraph 7.95 may be used to allow time to supply omissions; does not apply for deliberate omissions or where application is subject to a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete replies are processed per 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP § 714.03; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) in appropriate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to 1.105 requirements are governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136. Requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months for reply (applicant may extend up to six months). Requirements sent with an Office action receive the same period as the action on the merits. A requirement is an Office action for patent term adjustment purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply stating information is unknown or not readily available is acceptable. Requirements mailed without other action ordinarily set 2 months; use appropriate form paragraph 7.126 for standalone requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a requirement — narrow specification and limited scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope because it burdens both applicant and the Office; only warranted where benefit exceeds burden in obtaining information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify particular art area and particular claimed subject matter to avoid inviting large irrelevant volumes of information; indicate form expected (citations, copies, identification of collections, answers to questions, etc.). Prefer preparing requirement as a separate document attached or mailed so recipients can route appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format content of a requirement (¶ 7.105 and heading)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement must clearly indicate that a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement is being made, the basis for the requirement, and what information is being required. Requirements should specify art area and particular claimed subject matter and state why the requirement has been made and how the information is necessary to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.105 Heading should begin any requirement and be followed by explanation and additional form paragraphs (7.106–7.121) as appropriate; conclude with form paragraphs 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.105.01 — Stipulations of facts known to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to this requirement, please agree or disagree to the stipulation of each of the following assertions of facts: [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify each factual assertion as a separate numbered sentence and append '(agree/disagree)' to facilitate applicant marking up replies. Must be preceded by ¶ 7.105 and followed by appropriate concluding paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.105.02 — Interrogatories of facts known to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to this requirement, please provide answers to each of the following interrogatories eliciting factual information: [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify each interrogatory as separate numbered sentence; clearly set forth scope and characterize expected content as factual. Must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.106 — Domain of search
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to extend the domain of search for prior art; state classes/subclasses and describe the broader range of art to search necessary to establish level of knowledge in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert description of art claimed but not found in classification system. Must be preceded by ¶ 7.105 and followed by concluding paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.107 — Level of skill and knowledge in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to document the level of skill and knowledge in the art of [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to establish ordinary skill level; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.108 — Background description
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to complete the background description in the disclosure by documenting [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used where background in specification is incomplete; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.110 — Art suggested as relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to enter in the record the art suggested by the applicant as relevant to this examination in [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe where in application file applicant suggests art is relevant (spec pages, paper received date, relevant pages). Must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.111 — List of keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to this requirement, please provide a list of keywords that are particularly helpful in locating publications related to the disclosed art of [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps examiner extend search; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.112 — Citations for electronically searchable databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of citations to electronically searchable databases or other indexed collections containing publications that document the knowledge within the disclosed art of [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates searching outside Office repositories; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.113 — Copy of art referred to but not submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a copy of each of the following items of art referred to in the [1] that were not previously submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket, describe where in application file the reference occurs; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.109 — Products and services embodying invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The information is required to identify products and services embodying the disclosed subject matter of [1] and identify the properties of similar products and services found in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to connect claimed subject matter to commercial implementations; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.114 — Copies of publications authored by inventor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide copies of each publication which any of the applicants authored or co-authored and which describe the disclosed subject matter of [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner note: must be preceded by ¶ 7.105 and followed by concluding paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.115 — Art relied upon for description of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide title, citation and copy of each publication that is a source used for the description of the prior art in the disclosure, and a concise explanation of that publication's contribution to the prior art description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on (not all believed relevant); must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.116 — Art relied upon for development of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide title, citation and copy of each publication that any of the applicants relied upon to develop the disclosed subject matter, particularly as to developing [1], and concise explanation of reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on; insert description of most important inventive elements in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.117 — Art relied upon for drafting claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide title, citation and copy of each publication that was relied upon to draft the claimed subject matter, with concise explanation of reliance in distinguishing claimed subject matter from prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps assess whether drafting was influenced by prior publications; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.118 — Results of applicant’s prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether any search of prior art was performed; if so, state the citation for each prior art collection searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examiner insight into applicant’s own search efforts; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.119 — Names of products/services incorporating claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the names of any products or services that have incorporated the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify commercial embodiments; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.120 — Names of products/services incorporating disclosed prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the names of any products or services that have incorporated the disclosed prior art [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify attributes of prior art that most closely approximate claimed subject matter to narrow response scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.121 — Details of improvement over the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific improvements of the subject matter in claims [1] over the disclosed prior art and indicate the specific elements in the claimed subject matter that provide those improvements. For means/steps-plus-function claims, provide specific page and line numbers within the disclosure describing claimed structure and acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on; useful for assessing novelty and inventive step; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.122 — Submission of only pertinent pages when document is large
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a required document is over 50 pages, the requirement may be met by providing copies of those pages that provide the particular subject matter indicated in the requirement, or where not indicated, the subject matter found in applicant's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to reduce burden when large documents are requested; must be preceded by ¶ 7.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.123 — Waiver of fee and statement requirements for certain information disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 are waived for documents submitted in reply to this requirement, but only for those included in applicant's first complete communication responding to the requirement. Supplemental replies after the first must comply with fees/certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver applies only to documents within scope of the requirement and included in the first complete reply; subsequent or out-of-scope submissions are subject to fees and certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.124 — Contents of good faith reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is reminded that the reply must be made with candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56. Where applicant does not have or cannot readily obtain an item, a statement that the item is unknown or cannot be readily obtained may be accepted as a complete reply for that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should appear in conclusion of any requirement; clarifies acceptable form of statements about unknown/unavailable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.125/7.126/7.127 — Conclusions and timing wording
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.125 concludes a requirement that accompanies an Office action (reply period coincides with action); ¶ 7.126 concludes a requirement mailed without other Office action (shortened statutory period specified, ordinarily 2 months); ¶ 7.127 concludes an Office action that includes a requirement reminding that a complete reply to the Office action must include a complete reply to attached requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate concluding paragraph based on whether requirement accompanies an Office action or is standalone; include statutory period and extension information where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s obligation following applicant’s reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider the information submitted with the applicant’s reply and apply the information as the examiner deems appropriate. Identify which areas of search were used and which were not; indicate consideration of answers to queries and mark art that has been considered (initials/date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW processing, follow IFW Manual section 3.7. Art submitted within scope must be considered at least to the extent of IDS handling; if applicant provides a written list of citations, examiner must mark which art was considered. If no list provided, examiner need not prepare one unless relying on the art in a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope principle — consider only art within the plain meaning of requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is never appropriate to deny considering information submitted in reply that is within the scope of the 1.105 requirement. Information beyond the scope need not be considered unless submitted in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requirement text plainly defines scope to measure what is within/outside scope. Beyond-scope art submitted in accordance with IDS rules must be considered per IDS provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on making next Office action final relying on art submitted in reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinguishes practice following 1.105 replies from practice after IDS submissions under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98 and MPEP §§ 609.04(b), 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to requirements under 37 CFR 1.105 (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking withdrawal or modification of a 1.105 requirement or seeking to have information considered may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center where requirement was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition is not a reply—the time period to reply to the requirement continues to run while petition is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of 1.105 replies to Information Disclosure Statements (37 CFR 1.97/1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial reply responsive to a 1.105 requirement and submitted within the original time period need not satisfy fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98. Applicant should list references on Form PTO-1449 or PTO/SB/08 to have citations entered in the record. Subsequent replies must meet 1.97/1.98 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any submission of art beyond the scope of the 1.105 requirement is treated as a submission under 1.97/1.98 and must meet IDS provisions to be considered.
